decisions.decision: Citations were verified on 2026-10-22 once network access was opened: every DOI resolves on Crossref to the stated title, journal, volume, pages and year; arXiv physics/9905030 and 1310.1528 resolve on export.arxiv.org; NIST gives G = 6.67430(15)e-11 and Planck length 1.616255(18)e-35 m. decisions.decision: Library formulas are defined once in SI with physical constants as symbols carrying their SI value; "geometric units" means binding every constant to 1 (formula.geometric). gpuSafe and the GPU spec sample geometric units by default. Mathematical pi is the literal PI node, not a symbol.
decisions.rationale: Single definition for SI wrappers and GPU use. SI evaluation of e.g. planckLength underflows float32, so GPU safety is only meaningful in geometric units; a test pins that.

decisions.decision: to-tsl maps integer powers |n| <= 8 to multiplication chains, p/q = 1/2 to sqrt and 1/3 to cbrt (tsl.cbrt, not in the prompt list), other powers to tsl.pow. lt/gt used as values compile to select(cmp, 1, 0); select requires an lt/gt condition. The webgpu spec case is annotated and skipped when no adapter exists, so the webgl2 case is the CI gate. Float render targets were readable on SwiftShader, so the HalfFloat fallback was not needed. Locally the installed Playwright wants chromium 1208 but 1194 is installed; the run used executablePath with a throw-away config (not committed).
decisions.rationale: pow() of a negative base is undefined in GLSL/WGSL and x*x matches the JS evaluator; cbrt is exported by three.tsl.js r186; the rest keeps the semantics of the JS evaluator.

decisions.decision: WebGPU is exercised locally with a Playwright Chromium 1208 (Chrome 145) downloaded to a scratch directory, launched headless-shell with --enable-unsafe-webgpu --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader --enable-features=Vulkan,VulkanFromANGLE,DefaultANGLEVulkan --disable-gpu-sandbox. The preinstalled Chromium 141 cannot run r186 WebGPU render targets (GPUTextureViewDescriptor.swizzle is a string in r186 but 141 expects a GPUTextureComponentSwizzle), and other flag sets fail on canvas presentation ("A valid external Instance reference no longer exists", reproduced with raw WebGPU, no three.js). CI keeps WebGPU disabled, so the webgpu specs run only where an adapter exists.
decisions.rationale: S03 left the webgpu GPU case unrun; S04 needed a real CanvasTarget spike. Both now pass locally. Nothing under /opt/pw-browsers was changed.

decisions.decision: Spike result: on r186 two canvases on one WebGPURenderer, one with the cinematic pipeline (bloom, DoF, grain) and one plain, both present correctly with no validation errors. Pipelines are not shared: each view builds its own pipeline while its CanvasTarget is active (the prompt allows this).
decisions.rationale: CanvasTarget works on r186; the failure seen first was the Chromium 141 incompatibility in D-015, not CanvasTarget.

decisions.decision: Shared stage scope: opt-in per page (QGA_RENDER_OPTIONS.stage = "shared") and per scene (shared prop); pilots are AtlasStage and the two QFT field scenes. A scene with classic ShaderMaterial content or a shadow-casting light, or forceBackend webgl2, does not join the WebGPU renderer (it falls back to the WebGL2 pool or its own renderer). On WebGL2 a scene created out of view while the budget is full is parked with no context, and a scene out of view never evicts one in view; context acquisition is serialised. A scene that has its own onFrame decides whether it draws; the stage draws only views without one.
decisions.rationale: Shadows are renderer-wide state, so toggling it per view would recompile every frame. Parking and serialisation came from two defects found in testing: a victim evicted while still building crashed, and a redundant second acquisition deadlocked under a budget of 1 (regression test added).

decisions.decision: GPU time is resolved every 30 frames with renderer.resolveTimestampsAsync("render") (ms of the last renderer frame) and attributed to the view drawn last in that frame: exact with one visible view, approximate with several. The governor judges a window on GPU time only when every sample in it has one (gpuSlowMs 8, gpuFastMs 4), otherwise on CPU time, with the unchanged hysteresis and cooldown. The perf harness gained --render-option=key=value.
decisions.rationale: r186 has no per-view timestamp API. The numbers on SwiftShader (about 110 ms) are not representative of hardware.

decisions.decision: Four browser tests failed in the full run on Chromium 145: esm-runtime "non-WebGL devices" (passes alone, 2/2), smoke "bh" (software-rasterizer timing, also fails intermittently on unmodified main with the same 12 s wait), render-backends "delayed initialization plus rapid navigation" and "context loss" (both fail on unmodified main in this environment). None was caused by this change, and no test was skipped or loosened. They were not re-verified on the CI-pinned Chromium.
decisions.rationale: Compared against a worktree of main with the same config. CI runs the first three suites with a retry.

decisions.decision: The static-frame screenshot pair cannot be byte-identical: js/atlas-stage.jsx fills the starfield with unseeded Math.random (existing code, F-18/randomness rule, not changed here). The visual documentation reports a stage-off control next to stage-off vs stage-on and states that the measurement shows no stage-caused difference, not that the output is identical.

decisions.decision: F-21 stays open although the prompt lists it: the shared stage is opt-in and only three scenes use it, so most scenes still build their own renderer. S05 (which also lists F-21) closes it when every scene is migrated. decisions.decision: Scene3D `animated` declarations: true for the scenes that evolve while playing regardless of motion (QFT membrane, GR gravity well, scale corridor); "motion" for scenes whose animation their own code gates by the motion factor (Standard Model map, Planck descent and spin foam, RG flow, GW inspiral, QFT collision and vacuum lab, AdS and collider labs, Hawking lab, approaches); false plus invalidateKey for the GW lattice; isAnimated() for Kerr and the Planck probe glide. Under reduced motion "motion" scenes now settle on one frame and idle instead of continuing ambient shimmer. For animated={false} scenes cinematic drift does not keep them animating.
decisions.rationale: Idle static views must draw 0 frames. Ambient motion that the scene already freezes at motion 0 is exactly what reduced motion asks for; scenes with unconditional time terms (scale corridor) stay animated and are capped at 10 fps by the scheduler.

decisions.decision: View setup on the shared WebGPU renderer is exclusive: pipeline build, shader prewarm and pipeline swaps run through view.exclusive(), one at a time, with the frame loop paused. Found by scanning the views: with more than one view per renderer, scenes failed with "Destroyed texture used in a submit" / "usage includes writable usage and another usage" and fell back to static or WebGL2.
decisions.rationale: A prewarm awaits between activating its canvas target and drawing; another view's frame in that gap switches the target.

decisions.decision: The prompt says to delete the per-scene renderer path and also to keep ?stage=legacy for one release. Both cannot hold, so the per-scene path stays, reachable only through ?stage=legacy, QGA_RENDER_OPTIONS.stage = "legacy" or Scene3D shared={false}, and is to be deleted after one release. The Kerr WebGL2 GLSL path and the GR gravity well (ShaderMaterial) are served by dedicated WebGL2 renderers through the pool, as the prompt specifies.
decisions.rationale: The escape hatch is the more specific, explicit requirement.

decisions.decision: The WebGL2 backend does not reduce renderer counts (a WebGL context belongs to one canvas): the QFT view still has 4 contexts there. The 4 -> 1 target is met on WebGPU, which is the backend that can share. CI runs WebGPU disabled, so the WebGPU cases only run where an adapter exists (local, Chrome 145 SwiftShader per D-015).
decisions.rationale: Stated in the prompt's verified facts for S04; recorded so the measurement table is read correctly.

decisions.decision: Two line backends instead of the node path alone: the node Line2 (lines/webgpu/Line2 + Line2NodeMaterial) and the classic Line2 (lines/Line2 + LineMaterial) are both vendored from the pinned three 0.186.1 tarball. engravedLine picks per scene build, before the scene is built: node when navigator.gpu exists and nothing forces WebGL2, classic otherwise, for scenes holding a ShaderMaterial (GR gravity well, Kerr) and for a recovery rebuild after the node renderer failed. The prompt assumed CI runs the node renderer's WebGL2 backend; the code (create-renderer.mjs) draws every scene with the classic WebGLRenderer when navigator.gpu is absent, and Line2NodeMaterial cannot run there. Option 1 of the owner's recommendation; the owner then told the agent to resolve the open points itself. The explicit-fallback contract of the native WebGPU test (a scene that leaves webgpu carries the message "webgpu initialization/compile failed: ... Retrying classic WebGL2 once") is kept: the rebuilt scene re-posts the failure that triggered the classic-line rebuild into its new diagnostics entry (found when the first CI run of PR #57 failed that assertion; verified locally with an injected compile failure: all three scenes end on webgl2 with the message).
decisions.rationale: Zero THREE.Line is only reachable with a classic implementation. Scenes are built before their renderer, and a LineMaterial (ShaderMaterial) makes a scene classic-only, so the choice cannot wait for the renderer.

decisions.decision: Engraved lines always blend and carry analytic edge coverage. Line2NodeMaterial is NoBlending and fakes transparency by sampling the opaque scene; engraved lines use framebuffer blending with three's own factors (non-premultiplied alpha, additive as SrcAlpha/One), transparent-sorted, no depth write. The quad is 1 CSS px wider than the line and edge coverage is computed from the distance to the centre line on both backends; the pipeline-facing alphaToCoverage of the node material is off (it attenuated the edge twice: 2.5 px read 2.06 px). depthFade is a TSL opacityNode on the node backend and a patch of the vendored LineMaterial shader strings (onBeforeCompile) on the classic one.
decisions.rationale: The node WebGL2 backend, a pipeline scene pass with samples 0 and the software renderer have no MSAA, so edges were aliased and widths quantised; measured widths now agree with the request to 0.13 px (0.065 px on the real GR scene).

decisions.decision: Scope of the migration. All 29 THREE.Line/LineSegments/LineBasicMaterial sites are engraved lines; GridHelper (s3dGrid, RG grid) became engravedGrid and the ArrowHelper shaft in the GR scene was swapped for an engraved shaft; Line, LineBasicMaterial, LineDashedMaterial, LineSegments and GridHelper left the THREE compatibility export (NODE_TYPES keeps the line material names). Focal curves of 2.5 px: the hardest collider track, the QFT mediator line and the two merger trails. The other scenes have no single focal line: their focal curve is a tube mesh (AdS Ryu-Takayanagi geodesic, RG separatrices, Hawking temperature rail), which scales with zoom and stays a mesh, so every line there is 1 or 1.25 px. The GR strong-field annuli stay filled meshes as the existing comment explains. Picking uses raycaster.params.Line2 = 6 px; the annotation occlusion ray is given its camera.
decisions.rationale: The prompt lists only the THREE.Line sites; hairline helpers were the remaining 1 px lines in the same scenes. Tubes are geometry, not hairlines.

decisions.decision: Fixed a shared-stage race (S05 code, js/render/stage/shared-stage.mjs attach): the view was registered after an await, so when every scene was rebuilt at once (a render-preset change) another view's detach released the renderer and attach threw 'Cannot read properties of null (reading setCanvasTarget)'. Found because the native WebGPU preset test (qa/specs/render-backends.spec.mjs, the CI step 'real WebGPU API on a software adapter') showed scenes silently falling back to WebGL2 after capture to cinematic once engraved-line setup changed the timing. Also: an empty Hawking trail field (extremal spin) and an empty foam slice set no longer throw.
decisions.rationale: A latent bug of S05 made visible by S06; fixing it is required for the S06 acceptance and benefits main.

decisions.decision: Visual baselines: only the five captures that pass on unmodified main and fail on this branch were refreshed (bh-kerr-hero, bh-mobile-lab, exp-collider-event, qft-feynman-collision, rg-flow-field-3d). Seven more captures (approaches-theory-constellation, planck-scale-foam, qft-vacuum-lab, symbols-atlas, whitepaper, gr-causal-lab-simultaneity, planck-spin-foam-lab) already fail on unmodified main on this Windows machine (font and platform drift) and were not refreshed; the share of the engraved backdrop grid in them cannot be isolated here. The two page-scope baselines were regenerated with the spec's own --update-snapshots, because qa/capture.mjs does not hide the cinema bar that the spec hides. Visual specs are skipped on CI (QGA_QA_VISUAL).
decisions.rationale: Never refresh a baseline just to make a test pass; platform drift is not a line change.

decisions.decision: Environment: the repository had no .gitattributes, so core.autocrlf=true checked vendor/three and the prompt files out as CRLF and failed test/three-vendor.test.mjs and test/plan-ledger.test.mjs on Windows before any change. A .gitattributes (* text=auto eol=lf, binaries listed) was added and the tree renormalised (no content change in the index). The pinned Playwright Chromium (v1208, Chrome 145) was installed locally to run the suite as CI does.
decisions.rationale: The base was red locally for a reason unrelated to S06; without it the vendor integrity hashes of the new addons could not be checked on Windows.

decisions.decision: Kit scenes run on the node renderer on every backend. The prompt assumed CI draws node scenes on the node renderer's WebGL2 backend; create-renderer.mjs used the classic WebGLRenderer whenever navigator.gpu was absent or no adapter existed (the same gap as D-028). createRenderer now attempts "node-webgl2" (WebGPURenderer({ forceWebGL: true })) for a scene holding a kit material (userData.qgaNodeKit): after WebGPU when an adapter exists, instead of it when WebGPU is absent or WebGL2 is forced, never the classic renderer; the shared stage (forceBackend "webgpu") still takes WebGPU or nothing. Scene3D gained nodeKit (node engraved lines through requireNode, no classic recovery). Scenes whose only node-only content is engraved lines keep their D-028 classic recovery.
decisions.rationale: Without it a node-material GR scene cannot be drawn at all on browsers without WebGPU, which is where CI runs.

decisions.decision: Acceptance "no ShaderMaterial outside kerr-material.mjs" is met except js/visualizations/gw/gw-runtime.mjs (2 sites): the WebGL2 twin of the WebGPU compute lattice of the GW instrument. perf:audit ShaderMaterial sites 13 -> 8 (mod-gr.jsx 3 and the three-runtime.mjs compatibility export 2 removed); test/material-kit.test.mjs pins the allowlist to those two files.
decisions.rationale: The step list names the mod-gr.jsx sites; S26 ("a GPU spacetime field") replaces the GW lattice and its twin. Porting it here would widen S07 into the GW instrument and its audio-synchronised tests.

decisions.decision: The blackbody table holds blackbodyToSrgb(T).linearRgb, the peak-normalised linear triple that function returns, not a unit-luminance triple; brightness is the radiance factor. The table is half float (DataUtils.toHalfFloat) so linear filtering works on every backend without OES_texture_float_linear; the 1e-6 equality is asserted on the float32 table, the texture is within 1e-3 of it.
decisions.rationale: One definition of the colour on CPU and GPU: the test compares against the existing function rather than a second normalisation.

decisions.decision: Registered the compatibility lights (AmbientLight, DirectionalLight, PointLight of three-runtime.mjs) with every node renderer. They are subclasses and the node library looks a light node up by exact constructor, so every compatibility light was ignored ("Light node not found") and lit meshes rendered unlit on node renderers. Found when the GR scene moved to the node renderer. Also fixed in the move: two GR formula readouts read an undefined GR_BODIES, and the starfield and dust used Math.random (now seededRng; Math.random sites 35 -> 27). Visual changes of the GR scene (D-038): tone mapping now applies to the star, well and starfield (they bypassed it as ShaderMaterials), the well ramp uses design tokens, points are soft-disc sprites; the visual specs are local-only and were not refreshed here.
decisions.rationale: Correctness of the node path the S07 scene now depends on.

decisions.decision: On the node renderer's WebGL2 backend (transform feedback) a kernel reads its own buffers through the variable it writes, so a read placed after an assignment sees the new value, and two kernels (init and update) over the same buffers do not stay in step with each other. The particle kit therefore runs init and update as ONE kernel selected by a uniform, copies the previous state into locals first, and assigns every buffer exactly once. init and update are builders that return the new state instead of assigning.
decisions.rationale: Verified against r186 by the GPU-vs-CPU readback: with separate kernels or late reads a re-initialised run diverged by up to 4 units.

decisions.decision: Each particle system's kernel carries a per-system serial constant that changes its source and not its maths. r186 caches a compiled program by source and the program keeps the attribute list of the first kernel that produced it, so on the WebGL2 backend a second system with identical source computed into the first system's buffers and left its own untouched; a lab re-mount would have drawn stale buffers.
decisions.rationale: Found by the determinism test (a second system read back empty). Without it every rebuilt Hawking, RG, QFT or backdrop scene would break after its first mount.

decisions.decision: Tolerances of the GPU-vs-CPU test: 1e-4 on positions, velocities, ages and attributes after 60 fixed steps (the prompt's bound; Hawking and tracer positions agree to 1e-6, the reference system exactly), 5e-4 on the Hawking opacity (pow(sin(.), 0.7)) and 1e-3 on the QFT crest heights (24 cosines of arguments up to ~100 rad); the crest mask matches exactly. The reference behaviour uses a normalised cube sample instead of sin and cos for its direction.
decisions.rationale: sin, cos and pow are accurate to about 1e-4 on the software rasteriser CI runs; the bound is the platform's, not the algorithm's.

decisions.decision: Scope of the migrations. Moved to GPU systems: atlas backdrop stars (static seeded buffer, vertex-stage twinkle), Hawking pair field (the engraved trail segments became tail dots of the same system), RG flow tracers (a resampled float table, two texel loads), QFT crest markers (the closed-form mode sum), collider towers (vertex-stage rise about each tower's base) and every THREE.Points left in those scenes (one pixel on both node backends). NOT moved: the QFT waterfall surface (a mesh with a CPU ring buffer; S14 replaces it with the GPU lattice), the GW lattice (its needsUpdate sites upload the signal once per signal, never per frame, and its WebGL2 twin already deforms in the vertex stage; S26 replaces it), engraved-lines.mjs and the mod-planck, mod-experiments, mod-qft and extras canvases (line and 2D upload paths outside the six listed systems). F-27 therefore stays open.
decisions.rationale: Each of those is either not a particle system or is rewritten by a later prompt in the pack; moving it here would have duplicated that work. needsUpdate sites 38 -> 33.

decisions.decision: Every scene holding a GPU system or kit material is a kit scene (Scene3D nodeKit): the atlas backdrop, the Hawking, RG, QFT and collider labs now run on the node renderer (WebGPU, or its WebGL2 backend), with the node engraved lines and no classic fallback. Scene3D gained prepare(renderer) and compute(renderer, dt); compute runs on the session's live renderer only, a scene parked by the WebGL2 pool is not prepared until it has one, and a system seeds itself again when the renderer changes.
decisions.rationale: The three systems that reach the renderer through the session must survive pool eviction and restore; both defects were found by the shared-stage budget specs.

decisions.decision: Visual changes (visual baselines are local-only and were not refreshed): Hawking trails are dotted tails instead of engraved lines; the backdrop stars follow the shared glow profile and a slightly different twinkle (colour = base colour x (0.6 + 0.4 tw)); the QFT, collider, RG and Hawking scenes are now tone-mapped by the node pipeline; the QFT crest sprites show every crest rather than the first 24. Perf (docs/audit/s08-before.json vs s08-after.json, software rasteriser, desktop, p95 CPU frame ms): overview 316.6 -> 350.0, qft 350.0 -> 316.7, rg 333.4 -> 350.1, bh 766.5 -> 766.7, exp 283.3 -> 349.9: within the noise of a rasteriser-bound frame (quantised at ~16.7 ms steps); no hardware measurement was possible here.
decisions.rationale: Recorded, not hidden: the prompt asks for p95 deltas per migrated view, and on this platform they are not distinguishable from noise.

decisions.decision: Scope: every plot the prompt lists is on the kit, plus the Kerr radii map and the dielectron-mass histogram. Left on their own drawing because they are diagrams or live scenes without data axes, ticks or legends: the live strain oscilloscope under the 3D inspiral (GWStrainScope), the scattering-plane polar diagram (QFTScatterCanvas), the Feynman and causal-structure SVGs. F-06 (hand-rolled axes, ticks and legends) is closed on that basis.
decisions.rationale: The prompt's migration list is complete; the excluded drawings have nothing for a figure grammar to do.

decisions.decision: Behaviour changes from the migration (physics byte-for-byte): the Higgs vacuum marker no longer wobbles (decoration); the GW phase ribbon is three fill regions; the spectrogram uses the magma sequential map instead of the brand ramp and reveals columns up to the playhead without the 20 % ghost; the RG phase-line arrows are triangle markers; the Kerr radii map drops the sweep animation and the filled discs; the null-geodesic comet pulses are gone; the Newtonian V_eff branch is dimmed one level instead of the GR branch when the Newtonian view is chosen.
decisions.rationale: The kit allows only sequential or diverging palettes, no glow off emitters and no decoration layer on plots.

decisions.decision: Citations were checked against Crossref (DOI to title, journal, volume, pages, year) for all 12 DOIs used in js/figure/provenance.mjs; all match. Textbook section and equation numbers could not be checked offline, so Misner-Thorne-Wheeler is cited by chapter 25 and Peskin-Schroeder by section 5.1, chapter 2 or chapter 4 only. Luminet 1979 carries no DOI in Crossref and is cited by journal, volume, page and year.
decisions.rationale: The prompt requires every citation verified against the primary source; unverifiable detail was removed rather than guessed.

decisions.decision: 27 pigment tokens that only the removed canvas code used are deleted from styles/tokens.css (the no-orphaned-pigments test requires it; none is read by any stylesheet). The floor in the token-read sanity test goes from 400 to 300 because 38 reads left with the migrated plots (386 remain). Neither change touches a baseline.
decisions.rationale: Dead tokens must not stay; the floor guards against a broken scanner, not against fewer reads.

decisions.decision: Visual baselines are not refreshed. They are local-only (the visual specs skip in CI) and this environment cannot reproduce them: symbols-atlas, whitepaper and bh-hawking-lab fail against the committed baselines on an unmodified origin/main here. Captures whose content changed on purpose: bh-hawking-lab, bh-kerr-hero, bh-kerr-observatory(+mobile), bh-mobile-lab, gr-curvature-lensing, exp-gw-inspiral, exp-gw-theatre(+real, +mobile), qft-amplitude-room(+mobile), rg-flow-landscape-qcd, rg-flow-landscape-mobile-toy. Their one-line justification: the 2D plots inside them are now Figure Kit figures (title bar, nice 1-2-5 axes, legend, KaTeX labels). Refresh with npm run qa:update on the capture platform.

decisions.decision: Perf: scene build and canvas redraw run on change only (no per-frame loop). The GW strain and spectrogram panels rebuild their scene while the playhead moves; the spectrogram colour map uses a 256-entry byte table, so no per-cell allocation. decisions.decision: The running uses the two-loop equations (Buttazzo et al. 2013, Appendix B, eq. 96-99 and 101 without y_b and y_tau) with a leading-order matching at m_t (tree-level lambda, y_t with the 1 - 4 alpha_s / 3 pi factor, gauge couplings from M_Z, v and the MS-bar angle). The two-loop coefficients were verified by integrating the paper's own couplings at M_t (eq. 55, 57-60) to M_Pl and comparing with its eq. (61): lambda -0.0151 against -0.0143 (three-loop terms omitted), y_t 0.3831 against 0.3825, g1 0.6153 against 0.6154, g2 0.5054 against 0.5055, g3 0.4873 against 0.4873; the instability scale for those inputs is 4.9e9 GeV, inside the literature range. For the measured masses the zero of lambda is at 7.96e8 GeV (two loops) and 3.7e7 GeV (one loop), below the 1e9 to 1e12 GeV the plan expected for the one-loop truncation: the paper's own thresholds (lambda 0.1260, y_t 0.9369 against 0.1292 and 0.9498 here) move the zero from 3e8 to 5e9 GeV at the paper's inputs, so the cause is the matching and not the equations. The test asserts 1e9 to 1e12 GeV for the paper's inputs and 1e8 to 1e11 GeV for ours, and the figures and the provenance drawer state the offset. M_Pl = sqrt(hbar c / G) = 1.2209e19 GeV is derived from the SI constants (the plan rounds to 1.22e19). stabilityRegion is computed from this running (documented truncation, not digitised); at m_H = 125.13 the stable and unstable lines are at m_t = 169.2 and 176.3 GeV, and the measured point is metastable (lambda_min = -0.0228 at 4.5e17 GeV, log10 p0 = -265, H0 = 67.4 km/s/Mpc from Planck 2018).
decisions.rationale: Tuning the matching until the plan's range is met would be a tuned number; the honest result is shown with its cause and the test that proves the equations.

decisions.decision: The local formula-gpu failure noted in D-072 (twoFlavourOscillation, webgl2, 1.0636e-3 against 2e-4) is not a mapping bug. The Vulkan specification (appendix 'Precision and Operation of SPIR-V Instructions', table for sin() and cos()) allows an absolute error of 2^-11 = 4.9e-4 inside [-pi, pi] and gives no bound outside it. A single-function probe on the local rasterizer (ANGLE, SwiftShader Vulkan 1.3.0, LLVM 10.0.0) measured 1.89e-4 for sin(x) at x = 1.40, independent of the argument size. twoFlavourOscillation is P = sin^2(2 theta) sin^2(phi), so |dP| <= 4 x 2^-11 = 1.95e-3, and the worst sample was 7.2e-4 absolute at P = 0.95, not near a zero. qa/specs/formula-gpu.spec.mjs now compares formulas listed in TRIG_BUDGET by max absolute error divided by the output scale against that budget (7.5e-4 measured) and keeps the strict relative 2e-4 for every other formula; the raw relative error stays in the console report. Two other fixes were tried and did not change the number, so they were reverted: folding the sin/cos argument into [-pi, pi] in compileTSL (result identical to the digit) and a floor on the relative error. Whether CI's rasterizer has a more accurate sin was not checked; the spec was green on CI for PR 75.
decisions.rationale: The tolerance was written for float arithmetic, not for the specified accuracy of the shader's transcendental functions; the budget is derived, not fitted, and a mapping error still shows as an O(1) deviation.

decisions.decision: The null-geodesic panel of the GR view lost its travelling pulse when the figure moved to the Figure Kit (the CSS dash animation of the old SVG). It is back as photons released together as a plane wavefront on a shared clock: the integrator's fixed step, so capture, the lag of the near-critical ray and the order of arrival are the physics and not an effect (js/visualizations/gr/null-photons.mjs, js/labs/null-geodesic-panel.jsx; the panel left js/mod-gr.jsx, which shrank by 37 lines). The clock readout is t / t0 with t0 the crossing time of an undeflected ray (2 half / (v0 dt) steps). At the reference mass (b_crit = 0.528, GR_C2 = 27.04) rays with b < b_crit end by 0.83 t0; the ray at b = 1.005 b_crit winds 1.26 turns and leaves at 1.35 t0, the farthest ray at 0.96 t0, and the ray at 1.05 b_crit leaves later still (1.39 t0), so the caption states that bent paths are longer and does not attribute the delay to the winding alone. Wavefront lines joining the photons were drawn and removed: a chord between a few rays does not represent a wavefront. Play/Pause and a scrub slider are provided, the clock rests at 0.7 t0 under reduced motion, drawing stops off-screen and in a hidden tab. A 2x display exposed that the overlay canvas needed the figure canvas's CSS box (the backing store is at devicePixelRatio); qa/specs/null-geodesic-panel.spec.mjs checks it. Two new captures (gr-null-photons, gr-null-photons-mobile; docs/screenshots 33 and 34, new baselines, not refreshed) are parked at 0.7 t0.
decisions.rationale: The picture is about light in a curved geometry; letting the integrator's own steps be the clock makes the animation carry the result.

decisions.decision: The lattice steps with two kernels, kick (writes pi) and drift (writes phi), as the plan says, and a third analysis kernel once per frame; each writes exactly one storage buffer and reads the others, so no invocation reads what another writes in a dispatch (race free on WebGPU). S08's one-kernel rule concerns kernels that write the same buffers on the node renderer's WebGL2 backend (a transform-feedback pass swaps the buffers it writes); here none does. The gather is possible there through setPBO(true): r186 copies a written buffer to a texture after each dispatch and reads it with texelFetch, in a kernel and in the vertex stage. Verified against the CPU reference on WebGL2 and on a Chromium started with the SwiftShader WebGPU adapter (--enable-unsafe-webgpu --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader); lattice-gpu.spec skips the WebGPU run with an annotation when the browser has no adapter, and CI disables WebGPU. Three r186 facts were found by running the scene, not the harness: setPBO must be set when the buffers are created, before any shader that reads them compiles; a readback of a buffer no kernel has written leaves an empty backend record that breaks the first kernel to write it (dualAttributeData.switchBuffers is not a function), so readback answers phi and pi from the start state before the first step and needs analyse() for the display buffers; and a readback waits for all queued GPU work (2177 ms per call on a software rasterizer). The step length may change under the quality governor: the first kick after a change uses the mean of the old and new length (variable-step leapfrog), which keeps the half-step offset.
decisions.rationale: A fused kernel would race on WebGPU; each of the three facts came from a failing run and has a test.

decisions.decision: Reduced motion and CPU rasterizers (softwareRendererClamp, the rule the Kerr observatory uses) start the lattice at rest until Play, Step or a click, and the lattice is 128 x 128 there (256 x 256 otherwise). With readbacks throttled the running lattice still cost about 2.4 s per frame on the software rasterizer (p50 2117 to 2483 ms, p95 2201 to 2533 ms in scripts/perf/collect.mjs, against 100 and 133.4 ms before), which breaks the plan's gate that the QFT view's CPU frame p95 must not regress. At rest the view measures p95 117.4, 116.8 and 133.4 ms against 133.4, 1067.6 and 733.4 before (three runs each on this macOS machine, Chromium with WebGPU disabled; very noisy), first frame 6063, 1954, 3879 against 2382, 4012, 7413 ms, programs 35 -> 39. S08's own numbers (qft p95 316.7 ms on the CI Linux machine) were not reproduced here and are not compared. On hardware the lattice runs from the start; its GPU time was not measured (no adapter in this environment). The energy readout is taken at 40 times its own measured cost on hardware and only while at rest on software.
decisions.rationale: The gate is measured on the rasterizer CI has; a simulation that cannot run there is shown at rest and says so on the page rather than hidden.

decisions.decision: The plan asks for leapfrog energy drift below 1e-5 relative over 10^4 steps at dt = 0.1 a. The instantaneous energy of a synchronised kick-drift-kick state cannot meet it for any state with omega dt of order 0.1 (it oscillates at (omega dt)^2 / 8, 2e-3 to 4e-3 measured), so the test reads it three ways. Free field: the exact invariant of the scheme (shadowEnergy) is conserved to 3.6e-15. Interacting (lambda = 1, vacuum sample): the oscillation is bounded by 0.25 (omega_max dt)^2 and the drift of the mean energy between windows of 50 time units is 1.9e-5 at dt = 0.1 a (mean of eight seeds, up to 3.6e-5 for one) and 4.7e-6 at dt = 0.05 a, a ratio of 4.1: second order, with no secular drift (a state-dependent shift of the modified energy during thermalisation), so the plan's 1e-5 is met at half its step and not at it. The kink: a single kink cannot close on a periodic box, so it is the kink-antikink pair; the tanh solves the continuum equation and the lattice Laplacian differs at O(a^2), so the profile is polished by gradient flow to the lattice's own static solution (stopping at a few thousand rounding errors, about 1e-11: an absolute 1e-13 is below the rounding floor of the force and did not converge at a = 0.25); without it the analytic profile moves by more than 1e-6. vacuumLike also draws pi with <|pi_k|^2> = omega_k/2, which the plan does not state, so that the sample is the free ground state's Wigner sample. Initial energy is the CPU start state's, the GPU readouts follow.
decisions.rationale: The plan's figure is a property of a quantity the scheme does not conserve; the tests assert what it does conserve and the order of what it does not.

decisions.decision: Scope reading and integration. FieldLab3D became the GPU lattice laboratory (js/labs/lattice-lab.jsx); FieldLab, its one-dimensional fallback, became the CPU lattice in 1+1D without damping or tuned constants (js/labs/field-lab.jsx); the amplitude room moved unchanged to js/labs/amplitude-room.jsx, js/mod-qft.jsx 1476 -> 695 lines. The plan also names 'the vacuum lab': I read it as the one-dimensional field lab (its label is the vacuum <phi> = 0). QftComputeLab ('Vacuum fluctuations, computed': the Fourier-mode free field of js/science/qft-fields.mjs, with a disclosed cutoff) stays because it is a different, tested computation and the plan names nothing to replace it with; if the plan meant that lab, it is the deviation to revisit. The old Math.random kicks the plan mentions were already seeded (S11); a click is now the seeded Gaussian kick of the lattice. The budget the quality governor gives the lab is its raySteps dimension, the only per-frame cost dimension applyRenderQuality receives. Provenance: qft-membrane became qft-lattice-phi4 (effective: a classical field, not schematic), qft-field-kinds describes the CPU lattice, formula-lens-qft-lattice is new (53 -> 54 entries). The unused pigments azure-92, blue-23 and blue-21-c05 were removed from styles/tokens.css with the membrane that used them (a test forbids orphaned pigments). The cinematic shots keep their ids and the section id and space name of the lab; two titles and annotations were reworded. The readouts, notes and the card text use KaTeX; the energy of the readout is written with the shared sciTex helper of js/core.jsx, which replaced the Higgs lab's private copy.

decisions.decision: The mode sum, defined exactly: a Dirichlet scalar in 1+1D, omega_n = n pi c / a, regulator f(omega / Lambda) = exp(-omega / Lambda); E_out is the same regulated energy of free space over the same length a, hbar a Lambda^2 / (2 pi c), because outside the modes are dense enough that their sum is the integral over the density of states a / (pi c). Lambda is given in units of the fundamental frequency (10, 20, 40). The sum is added term by term, compensated, to n eps = 45 with a 5e6-term budget. The limit is the 1+1D scalar energy and is not the 3-D pressure; the lab says so.
decisions.rationale: The plan asks for the regulator and the continuum to be written down; the 1+1D limit differing from the 3-D result is stated rather than left to be read as the pressure.

decisions.decision: Sources and numbers. The LEP/SLD values are the ones printed in Phys. Rep. 427 (2006), doi:10.1016/j.physrep.2005.12.006 (Crossref: Elsevier, pages 257-454), arXiv:hep-ex/0509008, read from the arXiv PDF with pdftotext: A_FB^{0,mu} = 0.0169 +- 0.0013, sigma_had^0 = 41.541 +- 0.037 nb, R_mu^0 = 20.785 +- 0.033 (Table 2.13, without lepton universality; their correlation 0.131), Gamma_mumu = 83.99 +- 0.18 MeV (Table 7.1). The paper prints no sigma_mumu^0, so the figure's cross-section point is derived, sigma_had^0 / R_mu^0 = 1.9986 +- 0.0034 nb, and is labelled so on the figure and in the provenance. Gamma_Z is 2.4955 +- 0.0023 GeV from the PDG 2026 Z listing (OUR EVALUATION, read 2026-10-26, added to js/science/data/pdg.mjs), not the 2.4952 of js/physics.mjs and of the paper; M_Z and sin^2 theta_W are the PDG 2026 values already in the repository. The plan asks for alpha(M_Z), which PDG 2026 does not print as a number (D-069): the model takes 1/alpha = 128.945, printed in the introduction of the same LEP paper (Delta alpha = 0.05901 +- 0.00035 with Delta alpha_had^(5) = 0.02758 +- 0.00035 there; PDG 2026 has 0.02760 +- 0.00010, which moves 1/alpha by 0.003) and not computed. No figure was digitised and no value outside the tables was committed; the licence of the paper (Elsevier) matters only for its figures, which are not used.
decisions.rationale: The source wins over the plan and over the older constants in js/physics.mjs; a value that the source does not print is derived with its own uncertainty and says so.

decisions.decision: Model scope, stated on the figures and in the provenance: tree level, massless fermions, one fixed alpha for gamma + Z (the Z-scale value, so the 10 GeV cross-section is about 13 percent above the value with alpha(0); the QED processes use alpha(0)), a constant Z width, MS-bar sin^2 theta_W = 0.23122 and not the effective leptonic angle, no initial-state radiation, no loops. Against the pole values: the peak is 0.9 percent under the derived LEP pole cross-section and A_FB is 0.2 sigma from the LEP asymmetry; the tests allow 3 percent and one sigma. The zero crossing of the asymmetry is at 91.0075 GeV, 0.18 GeV below the pole, because Re chi vanishes at the pole itself: the figure marks it as the plan asks (the interference zero crossing), and the sign change below the pole is tested.
decisions.rationale: A tuned alpha or width would hide the radiative corrections instead of naming them.

decisions.decision: Bhabha, Moller and e mu. The plan's angular form of Bhabha equals the Mandelstam form 2 e^4 [(s^2+u^2)/t^2 + 2u^2/(st) + (t^2+u^2)/s^2] (checked numerically in the tests to 1e-12, and it is the s, t and interference sum the room draws); Moller is 2 e^4 [(s^2+u^2)/t^2 + 2s^2/(tu) + (s^2+t^2)/u^2], which equals alpha^2 (3 + cos^2 theta)^2 / (s sin^4 theta). Both were derived here from the helicity amplitudes and cross-checked against each other and the Rutherford limit; the plan names no source for them (it cites Peskin & Schroeder section 5.1 only for the pure-QED limit of the muon process) and a printed form in a textbook could not be read, so no citation of a page is made, the comment in js/science/electroweak.mjs says the formulas were derived, and the room's reference lines say the same. The e mu process now shows the complete massless result (s^2+u^2)/t^2 instead of the 1/sin^4(theta/2) pole.
decisions.rationale: A citation of a source that was not read would be a claim; the derivation is checkable in the tests.

decisions.decision: alpha_em^-1(M_Z) in the MS-bar scheme is derived, not taken from the plan: 127.961 +- 0.014. The plan's 127.951 is the value the PDG 2022 edition prints (127.951 +- 0.009). The 2024 edition prints 127.930 +- 0.008 (with Delta alpha_had^(5) = 0.02783 and alpha_s = 0.1187), which corrects D-069: that decision said neither the 2024 nor the 2026 edition prints it; the 2024 edition does, the 2026 one does not. A number from one edition does not go with the sin^2 theta_W and alpha_s of another, so the value is rebuilt from the 2026 inputs with the relation of the review's Section 10.3.1: alpha(0)^-1 = 137.035 999 177(21) (eq. 10.19) times [1 - Delta alpha_lep - Delta alpha_had^(5) = 0.02760(10) - (Delta alpha-hat - Delta alpha) = 0.007123 (eq. 10.21)], with Delta alpha_lep = 314.97686e-4 from Steinhauser, Phys. Lett. B 429, 158 (1998), Table 1 (DOI 10.1016/S0370-2693(98)00503-6 confirmed on Crossref, paper read; it quotes no uncertainty, so its three-loop term 1e-6 is taken as the bound). The check: the same pipeline with the 2024 Delta alpha_had returns 127.9299, the 127.930 that edition prints. The consequence for the plan's numbers: 59.024, 29.587, 8.475 instead of 59.020, 29.585, 8.475 (the plan values are reproduced by the explicit override 127.951 in the tests); 33.29, 49.46, 52.41 at the Planck mass hold to 0.01 either way. M_Pl is the 1.2209e19 GeV computed from the SI constants by higgs-running.mjs.
decisions.rationale: The prompt says an unverifiable number is not shipped and the source wins; a derivation that reproduces a printed value of another edition to 0.001 is the verifiable route.

decisions.decision: The coefficient tables are verified against sources that were read: the MSSM b_i and b_ij against Martin & Vaughn, PRD 50, 2282 (1994), eq. (4.4)-(4.5) (arXiv:hep-ph/9311340 downloaded and read; DOI confirmed on Crossref) and the SM b_i and b_ij against Buttazzo et al., JHEP 12 (2013) 089, appendix B.1 eq. (96)-(98), the coefficients of g^2 with the Yukawa couplings set to zero (arXiv:1307.3536 read): all 6 vectors and 4 matrices equal the plan's, and the code is checked against an independent integration of eq. (96)-(98) in g^2 to 1e-6. Machacek & Vaughn, Nucl. Phys. B222 (1983) 83 (DOI confirmed on Crossref) is paywalled and was not read; the prompt asked for it and that part is not met, nothing is cited to it as read. Martin & Vaughn do not print the SM matrix, which is why Buttazzo et al. is the SM source. Yukawa terms are omitted and stated; an estimate from eq. (96)-(98) with y_t(M_Z) = 0.95 puts them at 10, 7 and 5 percent of the two-loop gauge term at M_Z. The top threshold is not modelled (all six quarks run from M_Z; decoupling the top from alpha_em at M_Z would shift alpha_em^-1 by 0.18), nor the matching at M_SUSY.
decisions.rationale: The prompt says a matrix that cannot be verified is not written; both were verified against a primary source that could be read, and what could not be read is said.

decisions.decision: The Formula Lens is extended to Figure Kit marks in js/figure/lens.mjs, after reading js/formula/lens.mjs, js/visualizations/common/term-lens.mjs and js/linking/formula-terms.mjs. decisions.decision: The plan quotes g* = 0.707, lambda* = 0.193 and theta = 1.475 +- 3.043 i as Litim (2004). Read from the arXiv sources, they are the optimised-cutoff values of Reuter & Saueressig (2012) eq. (4.15)-(4.20); Litim's own eq. decisions.decision: The Penrose atlas draws its three panels at a common DRAWN HEIGHT rather than at one common scene scale. penrose-geometry.mjs layout() scales each panel so that all three are equally tall, and the scale stays uniform WITHIN each panel, so a null ray is still exactly 45 degrees on screen.
decisions.rationale: A conformal diagram is one coordinate system, so its R and T extents are set by the physics and the three diagrams are different shapes (Minkowski square, Schwarzschild two to one, the Reissner-Nordstrom block wider). One common scale made a band 13.03 units wide per unit tall; the desktop stage is about 5.7:1, so the framing could not fit it and most of the frame was empty. decisions.decision: Region III's time arrow is the image of region I's under the isometry (U, V) -> (-U, -V) of the extension's Killing field, so its i+ sits at (-pi/2, -pi/2) in the diagram, not at (+pi/2, -pi/2). schwarzschildBoundaries() places every edge and labelled point of all four regions accordingly.
decisions.rationale: The first draft put region III's future infinity in the corner its R coordinate suggested rather than the corner its time coordinate reaches; the diagram then had two future infinities on the same side. Fixing the corner is what makes the boundary labels agree with the region tests in schwarzschildRegionAt().

decisions.decision: The plan cites Penrose's conformal-infinity paper (10.1098/rspa.1965.0058) as the source of the diagrams. That DOI resolves to 'Zero rest-mass fields including gravitation: asymptotic behaviour' (Proc. R. Soc. A 284, 159), not to the singularity theorem. The module cites Penrose, PRL 14 (1965) 57, 10.1103/PhysRevLett.14.57 instead, verified on Crossref on 2026-10-27.
decisions.rationale: The plan's rule is that the source wins over the prompt when they disagree, and both papers are Penrose 1965, so the mistake is easy to make and easy to check. The conformal-infinity paper is not where causal diagrams are introduced; the singularity-theorem letter is.

decisions.decision: Minkowski's r is the SIGNED spatial coordinate of the 1+1-dimensional chart, not a radius: sampleCoordinateLines() sweeps a constant-t line over [-hi, hi] and draws a constant-r line as the pair of branches at +-r. The module header states the convention and test/conformal.test.mjs asserts the four polylines that two radii produce.
decisions.rationale: With r >= 0 only, every constant-t line covered the right half of the diamond and the left i0 did not exist, so the picture was a triangle pretending to be a diamond. Signed r is also what gives the constant-r lines the familiar hyperbola shape, since a fixed radius in 1+1 dimensions means r^2 = x^2.

decisions.decision: The Reissner-Nordstrom panel draws its block as a chain of three regions along the axis -- the triangle 0 < r < r- against the singularity, the diamond r- < r < r+, and the diamond r > r+ onto i0 -- and mirrors the whole chain through R = 0. Its extent is measured from the vertices it draws rather than quoted.
decisions.rationale: The first build drew each surface independently from a null-line helper and the result was four disconnected X shapes, with the singularity floating free. Building regions and deriving their shared edges is what makes the horizon crossings actual crossings. The extent has to be measured because the scene scales a panel to a common drawn height: an extent of 1.0 where the block reaches 1.55 blew the panel up to four times its correct size.

decisions.decision: The coordinate families are drawn in the chart of EACH of Schwarzschild's four regions, and sampleCoordinateLines() takes region-aware sweep defaults: r in [1e-6, 0.999*2M] inside the horizon and [1.01*2M, 22M] outside it.
decisions.rationale: The sampler defaulted to rMin = 2.004M for every region, so the constant-t lines of regions II and IV -- where r < 2M by definition -- were drawn with r > 2M and landed in region I. A test now asserts that every coordinate line of a chart stays inside that chart (schwarzschildRegionAt(p) === region).

decisions.decision: The lab derives its stage height from the drawn aspect of the atlas (geometry.stageHeight(width)) instead of a fixed 520 px, and the framing reserves LABEL_PAD of scene units above the band for the panel titles.

Three projected labels also need a row of their own: a projected label is offset upward by -130 percent of its own height, so a title placed at the band's edge hung above the stage. decisions.decision: The panel titles and the schematic note are DOM in the stage overlay, laid out by CSS, not projected labels.
